A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PURPLE research work. The complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original LaMP and LongLaMP experiments, ablations, throughput and ordering analyses, and a 250-instance human evaluation.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a profile-size sensitivity experiment in Section 5.5.

M1.justification: Both versions retain Contriever embeddings, query–record cross-attention, the inter-record Transformer, Plackett–Luce sampling, normalized log-likelihood rewards, and top-K inference. The revised attribution of order sensitivity clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six LaMP and three LongLaMP tasks. The new sensitivity study uses the existing Tweet task; varying profile size does not add dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain BM25, Contriever, IC-RALM, REPLUG, both RankGPT configurations, and ICR. The new sensitivity study reuses ICR. Newly cited ListT5 and EBCAR are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 adds evaluation at K=5, 10, and 15 on Tweet with Phi-4-Mini-Instruct, holding the candidate pool at 20. Existing benchmark settings, ordering controls, and the human-evaluation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.5 and Figure 5 test sensitivity to the number of selected records. This adds a targeted examination of whether larger profiles help; the existing architecture/reward ablations, ordering analysis, and qualitative case study are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain means and standard deviations over three generation seeds, with a single run for GPT-5-nano. The new sensitivity plot introduces no additional seed information, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds profile-size results: at K=10/15, PURPLE's ROUGE-1 scores are 38.9/38.7 versus ICR's 38.4/38.3. At K=15, both score 35.7 on METEOR. Tables 1–3, the earlier plots, and the human preference result of 57.2% versus 42.8% remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The ordered-profile definition, Equations 1–6, gradient estimator, reward normalization, and Jensen/ELBO argument are retained. The corrected Appendix A equation reference and changed LLM notation do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions and effectiveness/efficiency claims across nine tasks remain the same. The abstract's replacement of 'set generation' with 'order-sensitive generation' aligns its wording with the ordered-profile formulation already explicit in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 attributes order sensitivity to the PL model rather than the record encoder and replaces sparse/dense reward language with a semantic-granularity explanation. Section 5.5 adds an interpretation of larger-profile degradation as redundancy or interference. Existing supervision and transfer limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D removes the explicit statement that PURPLE training uses the same GPUs as LLM deployment. The remaining hyperparameters, inference hardware, precision, and code link are retained; the omission does not establish an actual hardware change.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds ListT5 (Yoon et al., 2024) and EBCAR (Yuan et al., 2026) to the listwise-reranking discussion and explicitly acknowledges PEFT's cost reduction. The central positioning around utility rather than relevance remains unchanged; other reference updates concern existing works.

P1.justification: V2 refines prose throughout, particularly Related work, standardizes profile and reward terminology, corrects the gradient-estimator cross-reference, and updates affiliations. Section 5.5 is added, while the existing section sequence and overall narrative are preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel sensitivity Figure 5, slightly rescales Figure 1, relocates Table 1 and Figure 3, and reflows appendix material. The earlier throughput Figure 5 is retained as Figure 6. All three table bodies and the existing graphical content are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity study provides useful evidence about the previously fixed profile-size choice, while the revised PL explanation improves internal consistency. These modest gains outweigh limited drawbacks: the new study covers one task/model, its blanket outperformance wording overlooks the METEOR tie at K=15, and Appendix D loses an explicit training-hardware statement. The main evidence and limitations otherwise remain unchanged.
